why_it_matters: Granting roles to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers allows unauthenticated internet clients or any valid GCP account to access bucket contents.
Attackers probe bucket endpoints using Cloud Storage JSON and XML APIs without credentials to list, download, or exfiltrate sensitive files.
Restricting IAM members to authorized service accounts or domain groups ensures that every read request enforces identity verification.
post_en:
You apply an IAM member grant with member = "allUsers".
Step 1: An anonymous scanner probes your Cloud Storage bucket URL over HTTPS using the standard XML API.
Step 2: The storage service responds with object metadata and download endpoints without requiring any authentication token.
Step 3: The attacker enumerates and downloads every stored object directly across the public internet.
CKV_GCP_28 fails when a bucket IAM policy grants access to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers.
Restrict access by setting the member argument to a specific user, group, or service account such as group:dev-team@example.com.
Would your CI pipeline catch this public bucket grant before it reaches production?
